flags.detail: Option C ('Its entries pace out the sales month by month, showing how slowly material of this kind moved') is the only distractor in this item that the transcript does not contradict; it is partly SUPPORTED by the span 'Its months run at an even pace, with no slow seasons to read'. The first half of C — entries pacing the sales out month by month — is exactly what 'its months run at an even pace' asserts. The refutation has to come from the qualifier 'with no slow seasons to read', which denies a SEASONAL signal, not an overall pace; C's claim is about how slowly material moved, a different proposition. A listener hearing this once has an option whose wording echoes the transcript's own words and no incompatible assertion to kill it — unlike B ('blank stretches match the permit-suspension years' vs 'the permit-suspension years are, oddly, the book's busiest') and D ('silent partner ... papers may still be in family hands' vs 'he is named on the first page, and his papers came to us in nineteen forty'), both of which are flatly contradicted. Only the rhetorical frame ('That muddle has a cause') distinguishes A from C, not a factual refutation.
